name: The Phantom of the Opera
description: A disfigured musical genius haunting the Paris Opera House

film.title: The Phantom of the Opera
film.note: The masked-ball sequence was shot in early two-colour Technicolor.

legend: Leroux was a journalist, and he wove real details of the Palais Garnier into his tale. Beneath the opera house sits a vast water tank, built because the foundations kept flooding, which became the Phantom's underground lake. In 1896 a counterweight of the great chandelier fell during a performance and killed a member of the audience, and Leroux turned the accident into his most famous scene.

myths.claim: There really is a body of water beneath the Paris Opera.
myths.explanation: Builders created a huge water reservoir to steady the foundations, and it is still used today for firefighters' diving practice.

myths.claim: The chandelier disaster was inspired by a real accident.
myths.explanation: In 1896 a counterweight from the chandelier crashed into the seats and killed a spectator.

myths.claim: In Leroux's novel, only half of Erik's face is disfigured.
myths.explanation: Leroux describes a face like a death's head. The famous half-mask comes from the 1986 stage musical.

myths.claim: Lon Chaney designed his own Phantom makeup.
myths.explanation: The 'Man of a Thousand Faces' built the skull-like look himself and kept it secret until the film was released.

quotes.speaker: Narrator
quotes.source: The Phantom of the Opera (1911 English translation), prologue

legacy: Phantom of the Opera (1943), Universal's Technicolor remake with Claude Rains
Hammer's The Phantom of the Opera (1962)
Andrew Lloyd Webber's stage musical (1986), Broadway's longest-running show
facts: The Phantom's real name is Erik
He lives beside an underground lake beneath the Paris Opera
Erik is a master of music, magic and architecture
Lon Chaney created his own makeup and kept it secret until the premiere
He falls in love with Christine Daaé, a young soprano
The masked-ball scene was filmed in early two-colour Technicolor
Universal's opera house set on Stage 28 stood until 2014
hostIntro: Take your seats, the overture is starting. Tonight's feature is a silent picture, so you'll have to scream extra loud.
